Job Description:
Start date: September 2027
Location: Belfast
Duration: 36 months
Closing date for applications: 20th December 2026
Salary: A competitive starting salary of £16,632.00
36 hours per week // Pension scheme // Success share // Plus many more flexible benefits! // Fridays afternoon off
About us:
Ready to build the wings that lift the world? Join Airbus as a Craft Engineering Apprentice at our site in Belfast and play a vital role in manufacturing the wings and the mid fuselage for our A220 aircraft. This 36-month programme offers valuable hands-on training, recognised qualifications, and a clear path to a rewarding career in aviation.
At Airbus, we believe a diverse workforce drives innovation. We're committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to thrive. Airbus is a global pioneer in the aerospace industry, leading the way in designing, manufacturing, and delivering aerospace products across Commercial Aircraft, Helicopters, Defence, and Space sectors.
As the global centre of excellence for A220 wing manufacturing and a production hub for the A220 mid fuselage, our Belfast site delivers over 70 wing sets each year.
Our apprenticeship programme is carefully designed to give you valuable practical training alongside your academic studies, setting you up for success and helping your career truly fly.
With over 157,000 employees worldwide and as the largest aeronautics and space company in Europe, Airbus is at the forefront of the aviation industry. During your apprenticeship you will work alongside our experienced fitters and engineers to support you to complete the work safely and efficiently.
What you will be doing:
As a Craft Apprentice you’ll immerse yourself for the first 12 months of the programme learning the foundational skills required for building aircraft. While completing your academic studies the course will also cover an element of mechanical fitting activities.
This programme is designed to equip you with valuable qualifications and competencies to work directly on aircraft components.
This 36-month apprenticeship is structured to maximise your learning and
impact:
Year One: You will spend the first 12 months of your apprenticeship based at the newly renovated Castlereagh Campus of the Belfast Met working towards obtaining:
• NVQ Level 2 Diploma in Performing Engineering Operations;
• Level 2 Academic Qualification;
• Level 2 Essential Skills.
This will allow you to develop the necessary skills, knowledge and experience to enable you to make an immediate contribution when you enter the workforce in the second year.
Year 2 and 3:  Your Learning Takes Flight at Belfast! Building on your foundational knowledge, you'll join our world-class team at the Airbus Belfast site. Here, you'll apply your skills directly to live aircraft projects. Your varied tasks will require a range of technical skills. This will include:
• Preparation & Setup: This involves meticulously cleaning, sanding, and masking surfaces to ensure proper adhesion and a flawless finish. It also includes accurately mixing paints and preparing spray equipment according to specifications.
• Application & Quality: Skillfully applying multiple, even coats of paint using precise techniques, while monitoring environmental conditions. A crucial part of the role is inspecting the finish for quality, making adjustments, and performing touch-ups, all while strictly adhering to safety protocols and equipment maintenance.
• Fitting Activities - This would include a placement in our single aisle and wide body business areas to perform fitting activities in our wing box production areas, these activities will include drilling and installing fasteners.
You'll continue your academic studies on day release, working towards:
• Level 3 NVQ Extended Diploma (Aeronautical Engineering);
• Level 3 Academic Certificate.
Upon successful completion of your 36-month apprenticeship, you'll become a Skilled Fitter, specialising in the assembly of both metallic and composite components to produce the wing box structure and the mid fuselage section of our world-class A220 aircraft.
You'll receive a Modern Apprenticeship Certificate, setting you up for a fantastic career.
Requirements
In order to be eligible to this apprenticeship you must:
Achieve a minimum of four GCSEs which must include:
• Grade C or 4 in Maths
• Grade C or 4 in English Language
• Grade C or 4 in Science or a Technology based subject
• Plus 1 other GCSEs at grade C or 4
Essential Skills, Key Skills or City & Guilds, at the appropriate level, will also be considered as acceptable equivalents
• Attach your CV (stating your predicted or achieved grades) and cover letter stating your motivation for the role and industry.
Applicants should be aware that the selection of successful candidates will be made in accordance with the eligibility criteria for the funding of the Apprenticeships NI 2021 program, as set out by the Department for the Economy.
BOOST YOUR APPLICATION
We want to get to know you! Not just your grades or school background so, tell us on your cover letter:
• Why Airbus?
What is it about Airbus that makes you excited to start a career with us? Is it our aircraft, innovation, global impact, or something else? Let us know what interests you about our work and why we stand out to you.
• Why a hands-on apprenticeship?
Why do you want to learn by doing? We’d love to hear what draws you to practical, skills-based learning.
• Show your hands-on experience.
In your CV or cover letter, include any hands-on activities or hobbies where you've used practical skills. These could be things like:
•
• DIY projects
• Building and fixing things
• Doing make-up or beauty work
• Tinkering and Tech Projects
• Building models
• Baking or cooking
• Others
Important Information:
GRADES:  Any offer will be conditional upon us receiving evidence of your required grades 24h after receiving your certificates on results day, in addition to completing all pre-employment checks and online forms.
SECURITY CLEARANCE: You will be subject to a BPSS (Baseline Personnel Security Standard) check. You may also need to gain UK SC-level Security Clearance or Export Control, depending on the role.
RIGHT TO WORK IN THE UK: Candidates must have current legal authorisation to work in the United Kingdom for the full duration of the programme. For more information, please check the Government Website. Our apprenticeship roles do not meet the minimum requirements set by UK Visas & Immigration to enable sponsorship of migrant workers.

Job Description:
Customer Success Manager - Jonas Event Technology UK
Company Overview
Jonas Event Technology (JET) is a leading provider of event registration software and services, supporting trade exhibitions, consumer shows, and conferences with innovative technology and exceptional customer service. Our mission is to deliver seamless event experiences through powerful SaaS solutions and a client-first approach.
We're the technology behind events. When an organiser runs a trade show, exhibition or conference, we handle the registration - visitors and exhibitors signing up online, badges printed and scanned on the day, check-in at the door, and the lead capture exhibitors use to follow people up afterwards. Our customers are the organisers themselves. Around 70 of them, across roughly 200 events a year, ranging from small conferences to trade shows with tens of thousands of attendees.
We've been doing this for over 30 years, and we're part of Vesta Software Group, which sits under Constellation Software. We're not a pure software business - we combine a registration platform with a full on-site service, with our people and our equipment on the ground on show day. That service is what we're known for, and it's why customers come back year after year.
The role
This is a retention and delivery role, not a sales one. There's no quota and no upsell target - our Account Directors own the commercial relationship.
Your job is to be the organiser's main point of contact, make sure everything they've paid for actually happens, and help them get real value from what we provide.
You'd be joining our Customer Success team, working alongside an established Customer Success Manager. You'd start with our smaller accounts and take on a broader share of the book over your first six to twelve months.
What you'll be doing
•
Taking the registration form brief from an organiser, checking it stacks up, passing it to our digital systems team to build, then making sure it's right before it goes back to the customer
•
Walking customers through the platform and the reporting so they actually use what they're paying for
•
Turning our product and feature updates into something customers understand, then showing them how to use it
•
Keeping proactive contact going - onboarding calls, regular reviews, post-event wash-ups
•
Tracking customer health, spotting when an account goes quiet, and acting on it early
•
Being the customer's voice internally. If something is frustrating several organisers, you're the one who tells our product team
•
Routing work to the right place - commercial conversations to the Account Directors, delivery tasks to the project management team
•
Keeping records accurate in Salesforce and Monday.com
You won't be building registration forms, uploading data or sending campaigns yourself. Those sit with other teams. Your job is making sure it happens, on time and correctly, and that the customer is looked after throughout.
What we're looking for
•
Experience in customer success, account management or client delivery, ideally in software, technology or a service business
•
Comfortable managing a high volume of accounts and deciding where your attention goes
•
Organised and reliable on follow-through. You chase things until they're actually done
•
Able to take something technical and explain it simply to a customer
•
Confident holding an honest conversation when something has gone wrong
•
Happy to be out and about, visiting customers and attending events
•
Comfortable with CRM and project management systems. We use Salesforce and Monday.com, and experience of either is useful but not essential
•
Events industry experience is welcome but not required. We're equally keen to hear from people outside the industry
Why this role
Most of our revenue comes from customers returning year after year, so looking after them well is the whole game rather than a support function bolted on the side. You'd be joining a customer success team early enough to shape how it works.
Practical
•
This is a hybrid role, with time split between working from home and our offices in Wallingford and Birmingham
•
Travel is an expected part of the job. Events take place at venues across the UK and our customers are based nationwide, so visiting customers and attending shows is a regular feature of the role rather than an occasional extra, particularly during the busy periods
•
A full UK driving licence is useful
•
37.5 hours a week

Lead From the Wheelhouse.
Svitzer is looking for an experienced Tug Master to join our Felixstowe operation.
This is not a ceremonial command. It’s a hands-on role at the sharp end of towage, where judgement, leadership, and ship-handling skill are tested every day.
If you take pride in running a safe, well-prepared tug, leading a crew that trusts your decisions, and working in close cooperation with pilots and port authorities, you’ll understand exactly what this role demands.
If that sounds like your kind of command, read on.
What the Role Really Involves
As Tug Master, you are accountable for the safe, efficient operation of your tug—every movement, every evolution, every decision.
That means:
•
Handling assisted ships safely and decisively in confined waters
•
Setting the safety standard on board and making sure it’s lived, not laminated
•
Leading and developing your crew, creating a culture of trust and professionalism
•
Maintaining vessel readiness, documentation, and operational reporting
•
Working closely with Port Managers, Harbour Pilots, and port stakeholders
•
Taking ownership of your vessel—because that’s what command actually means
This is practical seamanship, real responsibility, and leadership that counts.
Why Svitzer?
Because tug command should mean something.
•
1 week rotations – focused work, then proper time away
•
Modern, well-maintained fleet – no shortcuts, no compromises
•
A company that backs its Masters – trust, support, and clear standards
•
Global leader in towage with local teams that know their ports inside out
We don’t sell an easy job.
We offer a professional one.
What You Get
•
Competitive salary of £70,722.46 per annum
•
Permanent time for time contract
•
Pension matched up to 10%
•
Life Cover (4x pensionable salary) and Single Private Medical Insurance
•
7 days leave after 3 years’ service
•
Employee Assistance Programme
What You Bring
•
Master <500GT Certificate of Competency (minimum)
•
Valid ENG1 and STCW certification (minimum of six months on all certifications)
•
Harbour or terminal towage experience – essential
•
Experience with ASD and/or Voith propulsion systems
•
Strong communication skills and confidence working with multiple stakeholders
•
Solid administrative skills and comfort with computer-based systems
•
Ideally living locally to the Port of Felixstowe
•
UK Driving Licence & Own Car to be able to access the port
•
The right to live and work in the UK
This role isn’t about title.
It’s about earned authority, calm leadership under pressure, and doing tug work properly.
If you’re ready to command with responsibility—not just rank—this could be the right next step.
Building a Diverse Workplace
In Svitzer we value the diversity of our talent and will always strive to recruit the best person for the job – we value diversity in all its forms, including but not limited to gender, age, nationality, race, sexual orientation, disability, or religious beliefs.
